newsitem.title: UK: TABLE TENNIS-'KING' KONG KEEPS CHINA ON TARGET.
newsitem.headline: TABLE TENNIS-'KING' KONG KEEPS CHINA ON TARGET.

text.p: Unbeaten China remained on course to retain their men's team table tennis world crown on Sunday.
China recalled world champion Kong Linghui for the match against Croatia which they predictably won 3-0.
Kong was never seriously extended in scoring a 21-18 21-9 victory over 18-year-old Dragutin Surbek, named after his famous father who was European champion in 1968.
Italy finished runners-up in Group A to China, edging past Yugoslavia 3-2, thanks to two wins from former mainland Chinese player Yang Min.

The key positions in each of the four elite groups, in which the winners go straight into the quarter-finals and runners-up into the last 16, were virtually all decided going into the fifth and final round-robin matches.

Second favourites Sweden, still smarting from Saturday's 3-2 defeat against Belgium, bounced back with a 3-2 win over Romania despite the absence of former world champions Jan Ove-Waldner and Jorgen Persson who had lost out to the Belgians.

But the result was only academic with Sweden, who won the event three times between 1989 and 1993, certain to finish second in Group B behind Belgium whose 3-0 loss to Austria had no bearing on their quarter-final place.
That situation was mirrored in Group C where table-topping Germany suffered a 3-2 defeat against Poland while second-placed South Korea whitewashed the Netherlands.
The only real battle for the major places was in Group D where Japan won a 3-2 thriller against the Czech Republic to finish ahead of France, 3-1 victors over England.

Koji Matsushita was the backbone of Japan's success with two wins, but it was Hiroshi Shibutani's nerveless performance which settled the match. Shibutani, a solid defensive player, reverted to a looping attack against Josef Plachy to win the deciding match 21-9 24-22 after saving a game point in the second.
It was the third time Matsushita had come through in a crunch situation after handing out the same treatment to the French and the English.

The quarter-final lineup was completed in the women's team event where four places were up for grabs following the automatic qualification of elite group winners China, South Korea, Germany and Romania.
Hong Kong, bronze medallists in 1995, scored a 3-1 victory over Hungary while Sweden, Japan and North Korea also went through.
